journey.name: onchain accepted result
journey.description: Verifies that fixed-amount and send-all sends show success after the configured backend acknowledges the transaction, and that an accepted send finishes its local activity before a new send is admitted. Precondition: an onboarded E2E wallet on regtest with confirmed Savings funds sufficient for both sends and fees, a synced running node, and a second test wallet's regtest receiving address. Start with Autopilot coin selection. The wallet, recipient and backend must be test fixtures. The Max leg uses the existing Manual coin-selection route: an amount-less payment link followed by Max currently fails in Autopilot's Branch and Bound selection with CoinSelectionFailed before Confirm or native dispatch, even with confirmed funds. This journey verifies actual send-all acceptance through Manual; it does not claim that the Autopilot limitation is fixed or that fixture confirmation proves acceptance. Rejected or missing-result cases need controlled broadcast-refusal/response-loss fixtures, which the Capabilities table does not provide, and belong in Manual Tests.

actions.action: Hand the receiving test wallet address to the app with xcrun simctl openurl <simulator-id> "bitcoin:<test recipient address>?amount=0.00001"
If iOS asks whether to open the payment link in Bitkit, choose Open
Verify the Send Amount screen (id "SendAmount") is visible with 1 000 sats and Savings selected
Tap Continue (id "ContinueAmount"), tap Show Details (id "SendConfirmToggleDetails"), and verify the Confirm screen shows the receiving test wallet address (id "ReviewUri")
Swipe the send handle (id "GRAB") fully to the right
Wait for the sent screen (id "SendSuccess") and verify it shows the accepted payment amount
Tap Details (id "Details"), tap Explore (id "ActivityTxDetails"), and record the exact transaction ID (id "TXID") without selecting a different transaction by address or amount
Use the configured regtest backend to query that exact recorded txid and verify the acknowledged transaction pays 1 000 sats to the receiving test wallet
Navigate back from Transaction Details, then back from the activity to the wallet home screen
If the Wallet Backup introduction appears, choose Later (id "BackupIntroViewCancel") before continuing with the fixture send
Mine one block with the configured regtest fixture backend and wait for the fixed transaction's exact recorded txid to confirm before sending the change output

Open the menu (id "HeaderMenu"), Settings (id "DrawerSettings"), Advanced (id "Tab-advanced"), Coin Selection (id "CoinSelectPreference"), and choose Manual; return to Wallet from the menu (id "DrawerWallet")
Hand the receiving test wallet address to the app again with xcrun simctl openurl <simulator-id> "bitcoin:<test recipient address>"
If iOS asks whether to open the payment link in Bitkit, choose Open
Tap the available balance (id "AvailableAmount") on Send Amount to choose Max, then tap Continue (id "ContinueAmount")
On Coin Selection, select all the fixture's spendable outputs with their switches, verify Total Selected covers Total Required, and tap Continue
Tap Show Details (id "SendConfirmToggleDetails") and verify the Confirm screen shows the receiving test wallet address and the drain amount and fee
Swipe the send handle (id "GRAB") fully to the right
If the Are You Sure? alert warns that the payment exceeds half the fixture balance, choose Yes, Send
Wait for the sent screen (id "SendSuccess"), tap Details (id "Details"), tap Explore (id "ActivityTxDetails"), and verify this send-all transaction has its own exact transaction ID (id "TXID")
Query this exact txid on the configured regtest backend and verify it spends the selected fixture outputs and pays the remaining balance minus the actual fee to the recipient
Return to Settings, Advanced, Coin Selection and restore Autopilot; stop recording and shut down only the task-owned simulator
